Limitations of post-training quantization for LLMs

New scaling law perspective introduced by 1.58-bit LLMs

outline.chapter_title: Background: Transformers, Quantization, and System Costs
outline.description: Provide foundational knowledge for understanding BitNet b1.58. Cover Transformer compute patterns, quantization concepts, and how memory and energy costs shape LLM efficiency.
subtopics: Transformer building blocks: attention, MLPs, and dominant matrix multiplications
Compute primitives: FP arithmetic vs integer operations
Quantization primer: weights vs activations, zero-point, clipping, per-tensor scaling
Post-training vs training-from-scratch quantization
Memory hierarchy and bandwidth: DRAM vs on-chip SRAM
Energy models for arithmetic operations and data movement
Prior work: 4-bit inference (e.g., GPTQ/AWQ), BitNet 1-bit architecture

outline.description: Detail the architectural components of BitNet b1.58, its relationship to BitNet and LLaMA-like designs, and the engineering choices enabling open-source compatibility.
subtopics: Replacing nn.Linear with BitLinear in Transformer blocks
Ternary weights and 8-bit activations: design rationale
LLaMA-alike components for compatibility: RMSNorm, SwiGLU, rotary embeddings, bias removal
Why zero weights matter: explicit feature filtering and modeling capacity
Embedding precision considerations (kept in full precision)
Compatibility with Hugging Face, vLLM, and llama.cpp

outline.description: Explain the quantization functions and scaling strategies used to realize ternary weights and efficient activations in BitNet b1.58.
subtopics: Absmean weight quantization: scaling by average absolute value
RoundClip operator and ternary constraint: mapping to {-1, 0, +1}
Per-matrix scaling coefficient gamma and numerical stability (epsilon)
Activation quantization: per-token scaling to [-Qb, Qb] and removing zero-point
Comparison to original BitNet activation scaling approach
Implications for implementation simplicity and system-level optimization

outline.description: Explore how BitNet b1.58 changes the dominant computations in LLMs and how specialized kernels enable speedups.
subtopics: From FP multiply-accumulate to integer-add dominated operations
Why removing multiplications reduces energy cost significantly
Matrix multiplication with ternary weights: structure and sparsity effects
2-bit kernel integration (Ladder) for efficient inference
Impact on throughput, latency, and kernel optimization opportunities

outline.description: Describe the training and evaluation setup used to compare BitNet b1.58 with FP16 LLaMA baselines.
subtopics: Model sizes considered: 3B, 3.9B, 7B, 13B, 70B
Training data: RedPajama (100B tokens) and 2T-token setting (StableLM-3B recipe)
Evaluation datasets: WikiText2, C4 for perplexity
Zero-shot tasks: ARC-E, ARC-C, HellaSwag, Winogrande, PIQA, OpenBookQA, BoolQ
Evaluation tooling: EleutherAI lm-evaluation-harness
Inference benchmarking: FasterTransformer on GPUs and 2-bit kernel integration
Metrics tracked: latency (time per output token), runtime GPU memory, throughput, arithmetic energy estimates

outline.chapter_title: Results: Accuracy, Perplexity, and Pareto Efficiency
outline.description: Summarize core findings showing BitNet b1.58’s accuracy parity and performance advantages over FP16 baselines.
subtopics: Perplexity parity from 3B: BitNet b1.58 matches FP16 models
End-task zero-shot performance narrowing gap with scale
3.9B b1.58 surpasses 3B FP16 with lower memory and latency
Pareto improvement: better accuracy-cost trade-offs
Interpretation: role of zero weights in modeling power

outline.chapter_title: Scaling Behavior: Latency, Memory, Energy, and Throughput
outline.description: Detail how costs evolve with model size and why BitNet b1.58 becomes increasingly advantageous as models scale.
subtopics: Latency scaling: larger speedups at larger model sizes (up to 4.1x at 70B)
Memory scaling: reduced weight footprint; embedding proportion shrinks with scale
Energy analysis: INT8 adds vs FP16 MACs; ~71.4x arithmetic energy savings on 7nm
End-to-end energy with increasing model size and 512-token sequences
Throughput on dual A100 80GB with pipeline parallelism: up to 8.9x higher
New scaling law equivalences: 13B b1.58 vs 3B FP16; 30B b1.58 vs 7B FP16; 70B b1.58 vs 13B FP16
Implications for deployment planning and capacity provisioning

outline.chapter_title: Training at Scale: 2T Tokens and Generalization
outline.description: Examine the 2T-token training experiment and its implications for generalization and data scaling with 1.58-bit LLMs.
subtopics: StableLM-3B recipe alignment for apples-to-apples comparison
Benchmarks used: Winogrande, PIQA, SciQ, LAMBADA, ARC-easy
Observed superiority of b1.58 across end tasks at 2T tokens
Takeaways: strong generalization and data scaling behavior of ternary-weight models
